title: MgF2/Al2O3 periodic Bragg stack with single defect cavity
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic Bragg mirror pair (MgF2/Al2O3) with a single half-wave defect cavity will achieve high transmittance in 255-280 nm while suppressing 300-1100 nm, provided the mirror pair count is sufficient to create a photonic bandgap that overlaps the visible and NIR stopbands.
design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflectors create wavelength-selective reflection through constructive interference of reflections at each interface. A defect layer breaks the periodicity and creates a transmission resonance within the stopband. MgF2 and Al2O3 both have low absorption in the solar-blind UV range, enabling high passband transmission.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 17 film layers
manufacturing_considerations: MgF2 and Al2O3 are conventional e-beam evaporable dielectrics
fused silica substrate matches sio2 catalog name
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer thin-film optics
Photonic bandgap theory for periodic dielectric stacks
Defect mode resonance in Bragg mirrors
expected_advantages: Low UV absorption in both materials
Simple symmetric topology reduces optimization complexity
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient stopband rejection with only 8 pair mirrors
Single cavity may produce narrow passband that does not cover full 255-280 nm range
Index contrast between MgF2 and Al2O3 is moderate, limiting stopband width
execution_request_english: Design a defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate. Stack topology: air incident medium, then 8 repeated pairs of MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) and al2o3 (MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) first from air side), followed by a single MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) defect cavity layer, then 8 repeated pairs of al2o3 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) (al2o2 first), terminating on SiO2 (Gao) substrate. Total film layers: 17. All 17 layer thicknesses are optimizable design variables. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Total layers must not exceed 30.
